name: Barbell Bench Press
summary: A foundational upper-body compound lift performed lying supine on a flat bench, lowering a barbell to the chest and pressing it to full arm extension.

setup: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes aligned directly under the racked barbell.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor and retract your shoulder blades, pinning them firmly against the pad.
Grip the bar with a full, closed pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and stabilize it directly over your mid-chest with straight arms.
steps: Inhale, brace your core, and lower the barbell in a controlled descent toward your lower chest.
Keep your elbows tucked at roughly a 45- to 75-degree angle relative to your torso.
Lightly touch your sternum without resting the weight or bouncing it off your ribcage.
Drive your feet into the floor and press the bar upward along a slight backward arc until your elbows lock out over your upper chest.
instructions.breathing: Take a deep breath and brace your torso before initiating the descent, then exhale forcefully as you drive through the sticking point toward the top.
cues: Screw your shoulders into the bench

common_faults.fault: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
common_faults.correction: Maintain muscular control throughout the descent and achieve a brief, gentle touch on the sternum.

common_faults.fault: Excessively flaring the elbows to 90 degrees.
common_faults.correction: Tuck the elbows slightly toward the ribs to protect the shoulder joint and recruit the chest efficiently.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the glutes off the bench.
common_faults.correction: Keep your hips planted securely on the bench while driving force into the floor with your legs.

precautions: Always wrap your thumbs fully around the barbell rather than using a thumbless false grip.
Set rack safety pins just below chest level if training without a spotter.
